_national.varieties: Qualitaetswein and Landwein only from the official list of Qualitaetsweinrebsorten (about 40 varieties). A single variety name needs 85% (EU rule). Wine without GI may not name varieties that have a PDO/PGI. Each DAC narrows the list.
_national.min_alcohol: Must weights in degrees KMW (Klosterneuburger Mostwaage, % sugar by weight): Landwein 14 KMW and at least 8.5% actual; Qualitaetswein 15 KMW, at least 9.0% actual, at least 4 g/l acidity; Kabinett 17 KMW, no enrichment, max 12.9% actual, dry (max 4 g/l, or 9 g/l if acidity within 2 g/l), no sweetening; Spaetlese 19; Auslese 21; Beerenauslese 25; Eiswein 25; Strohwein/Schilfwein 25; Trockenbeerenauslese 30 KMW. Praedikatswein at least 5.0% actual alcohol.
_national.max_yield: 10,000 kg grapes or 7,500 L wine per ha for varietal/vintage wine without GI, Landwein, Qualitaets- and Praedikatswein (9,000 kg / 6,750 L before the vineyard register moved to IACS). If exceeded, the whole crop may only be sold as wine without variety or vintage.
_national.ageing: Reserve (general rule): Qualitaetswein with vintage, at least 13% vol on the label, submitted for the state test number from 15 March (white) or 1 November (red) after harvest; Grosse Reserve / Grande Reserve from 1 November (white) or 1 May of the second year (red). DACs may set their own Reserve rules. Sekt Austria: at least 9 months on lees (bottle) or 6 (tank); Reserve 18 months, traditional method; Grosse Reserve 36 months.
_national.release: Praedikat wines: Spaetlese and Auslese may not be submitted for the state test number before 1 January after harvest; BA, Eiswein, Strohwein, TBA not before 1 April. Many DACs add later submission or sale dates.
_national.styles: Wein (no GI); Landwein (PGI, 100% from one Weinbauregion: Weinland, Steirerland or Bergland); Qualitaetswein (PDO: one Weinbaugebiet, state test number on the label); Kabinett is a Qualitaetswein category, not a Praedikat; Praedikatswein: Spaetlese (fully ripe), Auslese (unripe and faulty berries removed), Beerenauslese (overripe or botrytised berries), Eiswein (frozen at harvest and pressing), Strohwein/Schilfwein (grapes dried on straw or reed, or hung on strings, at least 3 months, or 2 if 30 KMW is reached), Trockenbeerenauslese (largely botrytised, shrivelled berries). Praedikat wines: no enrichment, no sweetening, residual sugar only by stopping fermentation, harvest declared and checked by an official must weigher. "Ausbruch" may only be used as Ruster Ausbruch.
_national.labelling: Origin hierarchy: Oesterreich > Weinbauregion (Weinland, Steirerland, Bergland) > Weinbaugebiet (generic PDOs: Niederoesterreich, Burgenland, Steiermark, Wien; specific DAC areas) > Grosslage > ortsuebergreifende Weinbaugemeinde > Gemeinde > Ried. A Ried name must carry the word "Ried" and the commune; from the 2019 vintage only officially decreed Ried names. Smaller units need 85% from that unit. Grapes from a DAC area sold as generic Qualitaetswein may usually only name the federal state. Bergwein: terraces or slopes over 26%. Heuriger: young wine sold to consumers until 31 March of the year after next harvest. Schilcher: rose from Blauer Wildbacher, Steiermark only. Gemischter Satz: white field blend from one area (Landwein or QW, Vienna has its own DAC). Gleichgepresster: blanc de noir.
_national.sweetness: EU terms: trocken max 4 g/l (or 9 g/l if acidity no more than 2 g/l lower), halbtrocken max 12 g/l (or 18), lieblich max 45 g/l, suess above 45 g/l. Many DACs are stricter (e.g. Weinviertel max 6 g/l, Leithaberg red under 2.5 g/l, Mittelburgenland max 2.5 g/l).
_national.other: The 2023 provision (WBV s.1a) letting the National Wine Committee classify Rieden as "Erste Lage" and "Grosse Lage" for DAC Riedenwein was annulled by the Constitutional Court (VfGH) in October 2026 because it gave the committee sovereign powers not covered by the Weingesetz; the ministry said no Ried had yet been classified under it, and the pending Weingesetz reform is to move classification into producer-group product specifications. The OeTW "Erste Lage" remains a private association mark. Sekt g.U.: Sekt Austria (one federal state, at least 9 months lees), Reserve (one state, hand-harvest, whole-bunch, max 60% press yield, traditional method, 18 months, max 12 g/l), Grosse Reserve (one commune, max 50% press yield, 36 months, max 12 g/l); "Klassik", "Cremant", "Frizzante" are banned on Sekt g.U.

src.title: news.at: VfGH stoppt Rieden-Einstufung durch Nationales Weinkomitee (Oct 2026)

at-burgenland.labelling: Generic PDO for Burgenland; DAC areas Neusiedlersee, Leithaberg (with Ruster Ausbruch), Rosalia, Mittelburgenland and Eisenberg. Burgenland may appear alongside most Burgenland DACs (it is mandatory on Eisenberg DAC with "Qualitaetswein").

at-carnuntum.varieties: Whites: Chardonnay, Weissburgunder or Gruener Veltliner (blends at least two-thirds these). Reds: Zweigelt or Blaufraenkisch (blends at least two-thirds these). Other quality varieties may make up the rest.
at-carnuntum.release: Ortswein and Riedenwein: submission from 15 March (white) or 1 November (red) after harvest.
at-carnuntum.labelling: Gebietswein, Ortswein (Goettlesbrunn, Hainburg, Hoeflein, Petronell-Carnuntum, Prellenkirchen, Stixneusiedl) and Riedenwein (15% blending from neighbours allowed). "Niederoesterreich" banned; non-DAC wines from Carnuntum may name only the federal state. Glass bottles only for sale to consumers (1.0 L and 2.0 L sizes banned).

at-eisenberg.varieties: Gebietswein: 100% Blaufraenkisch, no blending. Ortswein and Riedenwein: 100% Blaufraenkisch or 100% Welschriesling.
at-eisenberg.release: Gebietswein sold from 1 September after harvest; Ortswein Blaufraenkisch from 1 March of the second year, Welschriesling from 1 September after harvest; Riedenwein Blaufraenkisch from 1 September of the second year, Welschriesling from 1 March of the second year.
at-eisenberg.labelling: Communes: Deutsch Schuetzen, Eisenberg a.d.P., Hannersdorf, Kohfidisch, Rechnitz, Gaas. "Burgenland" with "Qualitaetswein" mandatory. No crown caps. Glass bottles only for sale to consumers (1.0 L and 2.0 L sizes banned).

at-kamptal.varieties: Gruener Veltliner, Riesling, Chardonnay, Weissburgunder, Grauburgunder, varietal or blended (Burgundian names only on the main label).
at-kamptal.min_alcohol: Labelled alcohol: Gebietswein 11.5 to 12.5%; Ortswein and Riedenwein at least 12.0%.
at-kamptal.release: Gebietswein submitted from 1 January; Ortswein from 1 February and sold from 1 March; Riedenwein from 1 April after harvest; Reserve submitted from 1 July of the second year after harvest.
at-kamptal.sweetness: Residual sugar (g/l) may not exceed titratable acidity (g/l).
at-kamptal.styles: Gebietswein light to medium, no oak; Ortswein medium, no oak; Riedenwein medium to full, light to medium oak allowed; no botrytis dominance.
at-kamptal.labelling: Gebietswein / Ortswein (12 multi-village communes: Engabrunn, Grafenegg, Strass, Hadersdorf, Kammern, Langenlois, Gobelsburg, Zoebing, Mittelberg, Schiltern, Schoenberg, Lengenfeld) / Riedenwein. Variety, brand and terms at most half the size of the origin. Only "Qualitaetswein" as extra term; "Niederoesterreich" and "Weinland" banned; vintage mandatory. Glass bottles only for sale to consumers (1.0 L and 2.0 L sizes banned).
at-kamptal.other: From the 2025 harvest, grapes must be certified organic or "Nachhaltig Austria" certified (exemptions for producers under 5,000 L of Kamptal DAC and up to 15% from very small growers). New ordinance BGBl. II Nr. 250/2024.

at-karnten.labelling: Weinbaugebiet Kaernten within the Weinbauregion Bergland; national Qualitaetswein and Praedikat rules apply. Landwein from these states is labelled "Bergland".

at-kremstal.varieties: Gruener Veltliner or Riesling (15% other quality varieties tolerated).
at-kremstal.min_alcohol: Labelled alcohol: Kremstal DAC at least 11.5% (from 2023 vintage), with commune 12.0%, with commune and Ried 12.5%, Reserve 13.0%.
at-kremstal.release: State test number from 1 January after harvest (Gebiets- and Ortswein); Reserve from 1 July after harvest.
at-kremstal.styles: Dry only. Kremstal DAC: no botrytis dominance. Reserve: powerful, a subtle botrytis or oak note allowed.
at-kremstal.labelling: Communes listed: Krems, Stein, Rohrendorf, Gedersdorf, Stratzing, Senftenberg, Furth, Hoebenbach, Krustetten. No Praedikat or Kabinett; "Niederoesterreich" banned; vintage mandatory; "Kremstal Reserve" on the front label. Produced and bottled in Kremstal unless notified. Glass bottles only for sale to consumers (1.0 L and 2.0 L sizes banned).

at-leithaberg.varieties: Red: Blaufraenkisch. White: Weissburgunder, Chardonnay, Neuburger, Gruener Veltliner or blends.
at-leithaberg.release: Submission: white Gebietswein from 1 February after harvest; red Gebietswein and white Orts/Riedenwein from 1 May; red Orts/Riedenwein from 1 May of the second year.
at-leithaberg.styles: Mineral, tight, little or no perceptible oak; primary fruit subordinate.
at-leithaberg.labelling: Only "Qualitaetswein"; Burgenland allowed; DAC capsule required; no crown caps, no 1 L or 2 L bottles. Ruster Ausbruch DAC lies within this area.

at-mittelburgenland.min_alcohol: Classic: 12.5 or 13.0% labelled; Ried: 13.0 or 13.5%; Reserve at least 13.0%.
at-mittelburgenland.release: Classic: sold from 1 August after harvest; Ried: from 1 October after harvest; Reserve: from 1 March of the second year.
at-mittelburgenland.sweetness: Max 2.5 g/l residual sugar; malic acid max 0.5 g/l (malolactic required in effect).
at-mittelburgenland.ageing: Classic: large oak or steel, little or no oak note; Ried: large oak or used barriques; Reserve: large oak or barrique, oak may dominate.
at-mittelburgenland.labelling: Only commune or Ried as smaller origin; Burgenland and Grosslagen banned. Glass bottles only for sale to consumers (1.0 L and 2.0 L sizes banned).

at-neusiedlersee.varieties: Dry DAC and Reserve: Zweigelt. Sweet DAC: any white quality variety.
at-neusiedlersee.min_alcohol: Neusiedlersee DAC (Zweigelt) at least 12.0% labelled; Reserve at least 13.0%.
at-neusiedlersee.release: DAC submitted from 1 February after harvest; Reserve from 1 February of the second year; sweet Spaetlese/Auslese from 1 January; BA/TBA (Reserve) from 1 April.
at-neusiedlersee.styles: Zweigelt DAC (steel or wood, no Ried name, variety mandatory); Zweigelt Reserve (large cask or barrique); Neusiedlersee DAC Spaetlese or Auslese and DAC Reserve BA or TBA, at least 45 g/l sugar.
at-neusiedlersee.sweetness: Reds max 4 g/l; sweet categories at least 45 g/l.
at-neusiedlersee.labelling: "Seewinkel" may be added for sweet wines from Apetlon, Illmitz or Podersdorf. Bottles of 0.75 L multiples/fractions or 5 L; DAC seal required.

at-niederosterreich.labelling: Generic PDO for Lower Austria. Wines from the DAC areas (Wachau, Kremstal, Kamptal, Traisental, Wagram, Weinviertel, Carnuntum, Thermenregion) may be sold as Qualitaetswein Niederoesterreich, but then without commune or Ried names (several DAC ordinances forbid smaller origins on such wines).

at-oberosterreich.labelling: Weinbaugebiet Oberoesterreich within the Weinbauregion Bergland; national Qualitaetswein and Praedikat rules apply. Landwein from these states is labelled "Bergland".

at-rosalia.varieties: Rosalia DAC: Blaufraenkisch or Zweigelt. Rosalia DAC Rose: one or more red quality varieties.
at-rosalia.release: Submission from 1 January after harvest; red with commune or Ried from 1 November after harvest.
at-rosalia.labelling: Ried or commune allowed; DAC seal; 0.75 L multiples/fractions or 5 L.

at-ruster-ausbruch.varieties: One or more white quality varieties.
at-ruster-ausbruch.min_alcohol: Must weight at least 30 KMW (TBA level).
at-ruster-ausbruch.styles: Sweet wine meeting TBA rules, made from naturally shrivelled botrytised berries picked selectively by hand, grapes only from the Freistadt Rust; produced and bottled in Rust.
at-ruster-ausbruch.release: Not submitted for the state test number before 1 April after harvest.
at-ruster-ausbruch.labelling: "Ruster Ausbruch DAC"; no other Praedikat or Grosslage; vintage mandatory; specific bottle seal; 0.75 L multiples/fractions plus 0.5, 0.25, 0.2, 0.1 L. "Ausbruch" is banned on any other Austrian wine.

at-salzburg.labelling: Weinbaugebiet Salzburg within the Weinbauregion Bergland; national Qualitaetswein and Praedikat rules apply. Landwein from these states is labelled "Bergland".

at-steiermark.labelling: Generic PDO "Steiermark" (Steirerland region); Qualitaetswein labelled only Steiermark may not name any smaller unit. The three Styrian DACs require hand harvest. "Steirischer Qualitaetswein" is a permitted term.

at-sud-oststeiermark.varieties: Hand-harvested; only Welschriesling, Weissburgunder, Morillon (Chardonnay), Grauburgunder, Riesling, Muskateller, Sauvignon Blanc, Traminer and blends. Ortswein lead varieties e.g. Kloech: Sauvignon Blanc and Traminer; Straden: Sauvignon and Grauburgunder; St. Anna: Sauvignon and Morillon; Gleichenberg: Chardonnay and Sauvignon.
at-sud-oststeiermark.release: As Suedsteiermark: Gebietswein from 1 March (Welschriesling earlier), Orts- and Riedenwein from 1 May after harvest; Reserve 18 months later.
at-sud-oststeiermark.sweetness: Max 4 g/l; Riesling and Traminer dry. Kloecher Traminer Ortswein may be dry or halbtrocken, or a Praedikatswein with no sugar limit.
at-sud-oststeiermark.labelling: Legal name since 2018: Vulkanland Steiermark DAC (formerly Sued-Oststeiermark). Ortswein communes: Kloech, Straden, St. Peter, Tieschen, St. Anna, Kapfenstein, Riegersburg, Gleichenberg, Oststeiermark. Glass bottles only for sale to consumers (1.0 L and 2.0 L sizes banned).

at-sudsteiermark.varieties: Hand-harvested; only Welschriesling, Weissburgunder, Morillon (Chardonnay), Grauburgunder, Riesling, Muskateller, Sauvignon Blanc, Traminer and blends. Ortswein lead varieties per commune approved by the committee (Sauvignon Blanc everywhere plus Riesling, Muskateller or Morillon).
at-sudsteiermark.release: Gebietswein sold from 1 March after harvest (Welschriesling earlier, submitted from 1 December); Orts- and Riedenwein sold from 1 May after harvest; Reserve 18 months later than each tier.
at-sudsteiermark.sweetness: Max 4 g/l; Riesling and Traminer must be dry.
at-sudsteiermark.labelling: Ortswein: Kitzeck-Sausal, Eichberg, Leutschach, Gamlitz, Ehrenhausen. Riedenwein from a registered Ried; inside an Ortswein area the Ried must be paired with that commune. "Steiermark" may not be stated. Origin at least 1.5x the size of the variety. Glass bottles only for sale to consumers (1.0 L and 2.0 L sizes banned).

at-thermenregion.varieties: Gebietswein: Rotgipfler, Zierfandler, Weissburgunder, Grauburgunder, Chardonnay, Neuburger, Blauburgunder, St. Laurent, Portugieser, Zweigelt (field-blend parcels allowed). Ortswein: same minus Neuburger and Portugieser. Riedenwein: Rotgipfler, Zierfandler, Weissburgunder, Chardonnay, Pinot Noir, St. Laurent. No rose or blanc de noir.
at-thermenregion.max_yield: Riedenwein 6,000 kg grapes or 4,500 L per ha.
at-thermenregion.release: Ortswein submitted from 1 March; Ortswein Auslese, BA, TBA from 1 May; Riedenwein from 1 July after harvest.
at-thermenregion.sweetness: Dry; red Riedenwein max 4 g/l. Ortswein may also be Auslese, BA or TBA.
at-thermenregion.labelling: Ortswein communes: Perchtoldsdorf, Gumpoldskirchen (no enrichment for its Orts- and Riedenwein), Tattendorf, Wiener Neustadt, Bad Voeslau, plus Baden, Soos and others. Variety and vintage mandatory; Grosslagen allowed. Newest DAC (2023 vintage).

at-tirol.labelling: Weinbaugebiet Tirol within the Weinbauregion Bergland; national Qualitaetswein and Praedikat rules apply. Landwein from these states is labelled "Bergland".

at-traisental.min_alcohol: Labelled alcohol: Traisental DAC at least 11.5%, with commune 12.0%, with commune and Ried 12.5%, Reserve 13.0%.
at-traisental.release: Submission from 1 January (with or without commune), 1 March (Ried), 1 July (Reserve) after harvest.
at-traisental.styles: Dry; no botrytis dominance; Reserve may show subtle botrytis or oak.
at-traisental.labelling: Only "Qualitaetswein" as extra term; "Niederoesterreich" banned; vintage mandatory. Glass bottles only for sale to consumers (1.0 L and 2.0 L sizes banned).

at-vorarlberg.labelling: Weinbaugebiet Vorarlberg within the Weinbauregion Bergland; national Qualitaetswein and Praedikat rules apply. Landwein from these states is labelled "Bergland".

at-wachau.varieties: Gebietswein: Gruener Veltliner, Riesling, Weissburgunder, Grauburgunder, Chardonnay, Neuburger, Muskateller, Sauvignon Blanc, Traminer, Fruehroter Veltliner, Mueller-Thurgau, Muskat Ottonel, Roter Veltliner, Gemischter Satz, Blauburgunder, St. Laurent, Zweigelt (Mueller-Thurgau and Fruehroter Veltliner may not be named). Ortswein: GV, Riesling, Weissburgunder, Grauburgunder, Chardonnay, Neuburger, Muskateller, Sauvignon Blanc, Traminer. Riedenwein: Gruener Veltliner or Riesling only. 15% other quality varieties tolerated.
at-wachau.styles: All hand-harvested. Qualitaetswein, Kabinett or Praedikatswein. Ortswein and Riedenwein must show no or barely perceptible oak; Riedenwein may not be enriched in any way. Rose permitted.
at-wachau.labelling: Three tiers: Gebietswein, Ortswein (communes listed in the ordinance, incl. Loiben, Duernstein, Weissenkirchen, Joching, Woesendorf, Spitz, Spitzer Graben, Muehldorf, Arnsdorf, Rossatz, Mautern), Riedenwein (commune plus Ried on the main label; no single-estate brands or fantasy names). Vintage mandatory; "Niederoesterreich" banned; commune and Ried names only on Wachau DAC. Production in Wachau, or in a grower's own winery in Kremstal or Traisental with registered parcels. Glass bottles only for sale to consumers (1.0 L and 2.0 L sizes banned).
at-wachau.other: Vinea Wachau (private association, members only, trademarks): Steinfeder up to 11.5% alcohol, Federspiel up to 12.5%, Smaragd at least 12.5%; all dry, white (Steinfeder and Federspiel also rose), no oak influence, Wachau grapes, certified sustainable. DAC since the 2020 vintage.

src.title: Vinea Wachau: Steinfeder, Federspiel and Smaragd

at-wagram.varieties: Gebietswein: Chardonnay, Fruehroter Veltliner, Grauburgunder, Gruener Veltliner, Gelber Muskateller, Roter Veltliner, Sauvignon Blanc, Traminer, Weissburgunder, Riesling, Blauburgunder, St. Laurent, Zweigelt (varietal, blend or Gemischter Satz). Ortswein: single variety of Chardonnay, GV, Roter Veltliner, Weissburgunder, Riesling, Blauburgunder or Zweigelt (no rose, no blends). Riedenwein: Gruener Veltliner, Roter Veltliner or Riesling. 15% tolerance.
at-wagram.release: Gebietswein submitted from 1 December of the harvest year; Ortswein from 1 January; Riedenwein from 1 March after harvest.
at-wagram.styles: Dry; white wines without dominant oak.
at-wagram.labelling: Ortswein names limited to listed cadastral communes incl. Fels, Feuersbrunn, Grossriedenthal, Kirchberg, Koenigsbrunn, Klosterneuburg (south of the Danube). Only "Qualitaetswein" plus either a brand or a fantasy name. "Niederoesterreich" and "Weinland" banned. Any closure except crown caps. Glass bottles only for sale to consumers (1.0 L and 2.0 L sizes banned).

at-weinviertel.min_alcohol: Labelled alcohol 12.0, 12.5 or 13.0%; Reserve at least 13.0%.
at-weinviertel.release: Submission from 1 January after harvest; Reserve from 15 March; Grosse Reserve from 1 November after harvest.
at-weinviertel.sweetness: Max 6 g/l residual sugar (Reserve must be dry).
at-weinviertel.styles: Peppery, fruity, no oak, no botrytis. Reserve: dense and powerful, subtle botrytis or oak allowed, own-winery bottling, no bought-in must.
at-weinviertel.labelling: Austria's first DAC (2002 vintage). Only "Qualitaetswein" as extra term; only a commune, Grosslage or Ried as smaller origin; "Niederoesterreich" banned; vintage mandatory; bottles must carry the committee's DAC capsule.

at-weststeiermark.varieties: Hand-harvested; Blauer Wildbacher (only as Schilcher rose), Welschriesling, Weissburgunder, Morillon, Grauburgunder, Riesling, Muskateller, Sauvignon Blanc, Traminer and blends. Ortswein lead varieties: Schilcher and Sauvignon Blanc.
at-weststeiermark.release: Gebietswein sold from 1 March after harvest (Schilcher and Welschriesling earlier, from 1 December submission); Orts- and Riedenwein from 1 May (Schilcher submission from 1 February); Reserve 18 months later (Schilcher 12 months).
at-weststeiermark.sweetness: Max 4 g/l; Riesling and Traminer dry.
at-weststeiermark.labelling: Schilcher at Gebietswein level is labelled "Schilcher Klassik". Ortswein: Ligist, Stainz, Deutschlandsberg, Eibiswald. Replaced the former Schilcherland DAC. Glass bottles only for sale to consumers (1.0 L and 2.0 L sizes banned).

at-wien.labelling: Generic PDO for the city of Vienna (about 600 ha). Wiener Gemischter Satz has its own DAC; the general "Gemischter Satz" term may not be used on Qualitaetswein Wien.

at-wiener-gemischter-satz.varieties: At least three white varieties from one Viennese vineyard registered as Gemischter Satz, harvested and vinified together; largest share max 50%, third largest at least 10%; 15% other Viennese QW tolerated.
at-wiener-gemischter-satz.min_alcohol: Without smaller origin: max 12.5% labelled (committee may raise it). With district or Ried: at least 12.5%.
at-wiener-gemischter-satz.release: Not before 1 December of the harvest year; with district name from 1 March, with Ried from 1 May after harvest.
at-wiener-gemischter-satz.sweetness: Dry; Ried wines dry or halbtrocken.
at-wiener-gemischter-satz.styles: White only, vintage-dated, no strong oak (unless a smaller origin is named).
at-wiener-gemischter-satz.labelling: Districts: Nussberg, Grinzing, Sievering, Neustift, Maurerberg (Mauer), Oberlaa, Bisamberg (Bisamberg-Stammersdorf). No brands, fantasy names or traditional terms; no crown caps.
